excerpt: Ghost Core is a $3,499 desktop computer that runs AI models at home, with no subscription. Specs, what it connects to, privacy, and alternatives.
content:
Ghost Core is a desktop computer built to run a personal AI assistant entirely at home. It runs open models on its own GPU, connects to your apps, files, screen history, wearables and smart-home devices, and builds up context about your life over time so it can suggest things before you ask. Ghost says the conversational AI and its memory never rely on a remote AI model, and that there is no subscription. Core also exposes an endpoint compatible with the OpenAI Responses API, so its local models can power other apps, scripts and agents.

Inside is an NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF Edition GPU with 24 GB of GDDR7 ECC memory, a 6-core AMD Ryzen 5 7600, 64 GB of DDR5 memory and a 1 TB NVMe SSD, in a brushed stainless-steel case. It ships with Qwen 3.8-Next, Qwen 3.8-27B, Gemma 4-31B and Muse-Glimmer-30B. You talk to it from a Mac, Windows or Linux computer or from an iPhone or Android phone. The price is $3,499 excluding VAT, and the first batch is scheduled to ship on 31 October.

Core is made by ZMJ, Inc., which trades as Ghost. Its about page lists Andreessen Horowitz, Abstract Ventures, Audacious, SV Angel and Z Fellows as backers. Core was hunted on Product Hunt by Rohan Chaubey and launched on 11 October 2026, finishing #4 for the day with 184 upvotes.

We have not tested Ghost Core ourselves. This page brings together Ghost's own product, support and privacy pages, its Product Hunt launch and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Dedicated desktop computer, used from Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android
profile.summary_short: A home AI computer that runs open models locally and builds context from your apps and devices
profile.video_title: Introducing Core | The Personal AI Computer
use_cases: Running a personal AI assistant whose memory stays on hardware you own
Getting proactive reminders drawn from your calendar, email, health and smart-home data
Serving local models to coding tools such as OpenCode or Codex through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Powering your own scripts and agents without per-token inference fees
Searching your own screen history and files with a local model

paragraphs: Rohan Chaubey, who hunted Ghost Core on Product Hunt, introduced it as a personal AI computer meant to keep your AI, your data and its context on your own hardware. The point of difference, he wrote, is that Core runs its models locally and keeps building context from your apps, files, screen history and connected devices, so it can act without waiting for a prompt.

He listed the hardware (an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell GPU with 24 GB of memory, 64 GB of DDR5 and a 1 TB NVMe drive), the local models including Qwen, Gemma and Muse-Glimmer, and support for wearables and smart-home devices. He pitched it at people who want local intelligence and control over their data, at $3,499.
launch_story.attribution: Rohan Chaubey, hunter, on Product Hunt

fit: want an always-on AI assistant without sending your data to a cloud AI lab
already run a home server or local models and want a ready-made box with a 24 GB workstation GPU
want to serve local models to your own apps and agents through a standard API
not_fit: want a cheap way to try AI: it costs $3,499 up front
need the biggest frontier models: it runs open models of roughly 27 to 31 billion parameters on a 24 GB GPU
don't want to manage permissions, connected accounts and data deletion yourself: the privacy policy puts much of that on the owner

pricing.intro: Core is a one-off hardware purchase with no subscription. Prices are Ghost's own, in US dollars.

plans.name: Core
plans.detail: RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF (24 GB), Ryzen 5 7600, 64 GB DDR5, 1 TB NVMe; 1-year warranty, 30-day returns, free shipping for the first batch

notes: Ghost says the first batch is scheduled to ship on 31 October and that Core needs no subscription.
An internet connection is still needed for web search, email and software updates.
Ghost's founder posted on X that the first batch had sold out; check ghost.ai for current availability.

alternatives.intro: Nothing on Product Hunt's alternatives list is a dedicated box like Core. The closest are apps that run local models or build context from your screen on a computer you already own. Prices come from each product's own page, checked on 15 October 2026; review scores are Product Hunt users'.

items.name: screenpipe
items.what: AI that records your computer work to power agents
items.difference: Software that captures your screen, audio and meetings on the Mac, Windows or Linux machine you already have, rather than a separate computer.

items.name: GPT4All
items.what: A private assistant chatbot that runs on your laptop
items.difference: Free desktop app for chatting with open models and your local documents; no continuous context or device connections.

items.name: NativeMind
items.what: Fully private, open-source, on-device AI assistant
items.difference: Runs in your browser on top of Ollama models on your own computer; it works with tabs, PDFs and pages rather than your whole life.

items.name: Littlebird
items.what: The AI assistant that already knows your work
items.starts_at: Basic $0; see its pricing page for paid plans
items.difference: Builds context from your screen, apps and meetings like Core, but as an app with a free tier rather than a $3,499 machine.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Lyzr, Snaply, Klee, Unsloth, remio and Local.

pros: No subscription: the hardware price is the whole cost Ghost lists
Models and memory run on the device, with no remote AI fallback for conversation or memory
A 24 GB workstation GPU and 64 GB of memory in a ready-built box
OpenAI Responses API-compatible endpoint for your own apps and agents
cons: Limited to open models that fit a 24 GB GPU
Online features such as web search, phone calls and email still send task data to outside services
Erasing Core does not remove copies on paired phones, computers or backups, according to the privacy policy

faq.a: A desktop computer that runs AI models at home. It connects to your apps, files, devices and wearables, builds context over time and acts proactively, with its AI and memory running on the device.

faq.q: How much does Ghost Core cost?
faq.a: $3,499 excluding VAT, with no subscription. It comes with a 1-year warranty and 30-day returns, and the first batch ships free.

faq.q: Does Core work without the cloud?
faq.a: Ghost says Core runs its AI and stores its memory locally, but you still need an internet connection for web search, email and software updates.

faq.q: Can I use Core with my own apps or coding agents?
faq.a: Yes. Ghost says Core provides an endpoint compatible with the OpenAI Responses API, so you can point tools such as OpenCode or Codex, or your own scripts and agents, at its local models.

faq.q: What can I talk to Core from?
faq.a: A Mac, Linux or Windows computer, or an iPhone or Android phone. It can also be given access to supported cameras, smart-home devices, wearables and apps.

faq.q: When does it ship and what is in the box?
faq.a: Ghost says batch 1 is scheduled to ship on 31 October. The box contains Core, a power cable, a cleaning cloth and a setup guide.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Ghost Core?
faq.a: Apps that run on a computer you already own, such as screenpipe, GPT4All, NativeMind and Littlebird. None of them is a dedicated machine like Core.
